chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a menstruating woman who hears the sajdah. He said: “If it is among the obligatory prostrations, then she should prostrate when she hears it.”
Because this narration is carried upon recommendation.

key_terms.السَّجْدَةَ: the prostration, here referring to the sajdah verse heard in recitation
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; the act is understood as recommended
key_terms.الْعَزَائِمِ: the obligatory sajdah verses that require prostration

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a menstruating woman hears a verse of obligatory sajdah?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for a menstruating woman hearing a verse of obligatory sajdah. It states that if the sajdah is from the verses of al-ʿazāʾim, she should prostrate upon hearing it, while the closing note indicates that this narration is understood as recommending the act.
